newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Akzo to fight pill restrictions.
newsitem.headline: Akzo to fight pill restrictions.

text.p: Organon, a pharmaceuticals unit of chemicals firm Akzo said on Thursday it would fight restrictions on the prescription of its oral contraceptives Mercilon and Marvelon.
"Organon is convinced of the benefits of these pills. In countries where restrictions were imposed, we are taking all appropriate steps to have (them) lifted," it said.

Germany's drug regulatory agency said Tuesday it was keeping its restrictions on so-called third generation low-dosage contraceptive pills, imposed last year after a British study said their use could double the risk of thrombosis.
But Organon said its high-selling third generation pills Marvelon and Mercilon did not raise the risk of clotting.

"More than 143 million strips of Mercilon and 800 million strips of Marvelon have been sold, yet our extensive product safety and surveillance programme gave no suggestions of higher risks of thrombosis," Organon's medical director Hans Vemer said in a statement.
It said that restrictions on the pills' use in the United Kingdom, Germany and Norway had not been adopted by the European registration authority CPMP.

In Germany, the low-dosage pills may not be prescribed to women under 30 taking oral contraceptives for the first time. Other brands affected by the restrictions include American Home Products Corp's Minulet and Tri-Minulet and Schering's Femodene/Femovan.
